title: Ingesting Data (2): Syslog and CEF, Azure Activity, Threat Indicators and Custom Tables

header.html: 1. Manage a security operations environment (40 to 45%)

Plan and configure Syslog via AMA and Common Event Format (CEF) via AMA connectors; configure collection of Azure activity logs by using Azure Policy and resource diagnostic settings; ingest threat indicators into Microsoft Sentinel; create custom log tables in the workspace to store ingested data
the official Microsoft SC-200 study guide (skills measured as of October 21, 2026) and Microsoft Learn

html:
1Syslog and CEF via AMA

Network devices, firewalls and Linux hosts send Syslog or Common Event Format (CEF) messages. A Linux log forwarder receives them and the Azure Monitor Agent sends them to the workspace.

Item Syslog via AMA CEF via AMA
Table Syslog CommonSecurityLog
Message Standard Syslog Syslog with CEF fields (vendor, product, severity)
Install first The matching Content hub solution The matching Content hub solution
Forwarder fact Detail
Software A Linux VM running rsyslog or syslog-ng; Python 2.7 or 3 required
Non-Azure forwarder Needs Azure Arc (Connected Machine agent)
Ports The daemon listens on UDP and TCP 514; AMA 1.28.11 or later receives from the daemon on TCP 28330
Roles Virtual Machine Contributor or Azure Connected Machine Resource Administrator to deploy; Monitoring Contributor for the DCR

Facility and severity in the DCR: you choose a minimum level per facility; Sentinel collects that level and all higher severities (LOG_ERR collects ERR, CRIT, ALERT, EMERG). The portal sets only a minimum; the API can list exact levels.

Exam tip

. Same facility in both a Syslog and a CEF rule duplicates events across the two tables. Fix it at the source or with a KQL filter in the DCR.

Validate with netstat -lnptv (port 514), tcpdump, or a KQL query on CommonSecurityLog. Data can take up to 20 minutes to appear.

2Azure activity logs

The Azure Activity log records subscription-level operations. Table: AzureActivity. It uses the diagnostic settings pipeline.

Method When to use
Azure Policy (a policy that deploys a diagnostic setting to send logs to the workspace) Many subscriptions or resources at scale; assigned at a management group or subscription
Diagnostic settings on one resource: resource > Diagnostic settings > + Add diagnostic setting > Send to Log Analytics workspace One resource
Policy wizard step Setting
Basics Scope
Parameters Uncheck Only show parameters that require input; choose the workspace
Remediation Create a remediation task so existing resources are configured too

The policy effect is DeployIfNotExists. You need Owner on the policy assignment scope. A policy-managed connector shows Connected only if data arrived in the past 14 days. Subscriptions connected by the legacy method must be disconnected first (Disconnect All).

Some resources write to AzureDiagnostics, others to resource-specific tables.

Exam tip

. Policy = scale. Remediation task = existing resources. A new policy assignment alone only affects new resources.

3Threat intelligence

Threat intelligence arrives as indicators of compromise (IoCs), such as IPs, domains, URLs and file hashes.

Source Detail
Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence connector Standard and premium (premium adds Microsoft IOCs and enriched OSINT)
Threat Intelligence - TAXII Imports TAXII 2.0 and 2.1 feeds: friendly name, API root URL, collection ID, username and password, polling frequency
Upload API (preview) An Entra app with Microsoft Sentinel Contributor at workspace level; client ID, OAuth token, workspace ID
Threat Intelligence Platform connector Deprecated (Graph tiIndicators API)
Bulk import Flat file (CSV or JSON) in the threat intelligence page
Fact Detail
Tables ThreatIntelIndicators and ThreatIntelObjects (STIX-based); the legacy ThreatIntelligenceIndicator stopped ingesting after July 31, 2025
STIX objects Threat actor, Attack pattern, Indicator, Identity, Relationship
TLP White, Green, Amber, Red
Refresh Indicators are re-ingested every 7 to 10 days and de-duplicated
Manage Defender portal Threat intelligence page (Intel management)
Use Rule templates named TI map ... to Microsoft Sentinel; hourly run, 1-hour lookback by default, alert when results greater than 0; lookback up to 14 days

Microsoft Threat Intelligence Analytics is a rule that cannot be customized; it matches CEF, Syslog and Windows DNS events against domain, IP and URL indicators.

Exam tip

. TAXII needs the API root and the collection ID. New tables: ThreatIntelIndicators and ThreatIntelObjects.

4Custom log tables

A custom table stores data that no built-in connector writes. Name ends with _CL.

Task Detail
Create Log Analytics workspace > Tables > Create > New custom log (DCR-based); choose or create a DCR, a data collection endpoint (DCE), upload a sample JSON, optionally add a KQL transformation
TimeGenerated Required; added automatically if missing
Plans Analytics (default), Basic, Auxiliary or lake
Roles Log Analytics Contributor (tables); Monitoring Contributor (DCRs)
Delete Custom tables only; Azure tables cannot be deleted

Logs Ingestion API: an app registration (with secret) posts JSON to the DCE or DCR endpoint; the DCR needs Monitoring Metrics Publisher for the app. The stream name is Custom- followed by the table name ending in _CL, the token scope is https://monitor.azure.com, and the transformKql source passes data unchanged.

Exam tip

. Custom table = _CL suffix, a DCR, a DCE and TimeGenerated. The ingestion app gets Monitoring Metrics Publisher on the DCR.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A firewall sends CEF messages to a Linux VM running rsyslog. Which connector and table should the SOC use?

  • ASyslog via AMA, with events stored in the Syslog table
  • BWindows Forwarded Events, with events in the WindowsEvent table
  • CAzure Activity, with events stored in the AzureActivity table
  • DCEF via AMA, with events stored in the CommonSecurityLog table
Show the answer

Answer: D. CEF messages are collected by CEF via AMA into CommonSecurityLog.

S2The same firewall messages appear in both the Syslog and CommonSecurityLog tables. What is the usual cause and fix?

  • AThe same facility is used in both rules; fix it at the source or filter in the DCR
  • BThe workspace is too small; move the table to the Data lake tier
  • CThe agent version is old; reinstall the legacy Log Analytics agent
  • DThe TAXII feed is duplicating records; remove the polling frequency
Show the answer

Answer: A. Sending the same facility to Syslog and CEF duplicates rows, so fix it at the source or with a DCR KQL filter.

S3An organization with 200 subscriptions needs the Azure Activity log in Sentinel, including subscriptions that already exist. What is the best approach?

  • AAssign an Azure Policy at the management group and create a remediation task
  • BAdd a diagnostic setting by hand on each of the 200 subscriptions
  • CDeploy a Syslog forwarder in each subscription that streams the log
  • DCreate a custom table and upload a CSV file every night by script
Show the answer

Answer: A. Policy scales across subscriptions and a remediation task configures existing ones.

S4A partner shares indicators from a TAXII 2.1 server. Which information is needed in the TAXII connector?

  • AThe workspace key and the agent version number
  • BThe data collection endpoint and the DCR immutable ID
  • CThe API root URL and the collection ID of the feed
  • DThe facility, the severity and the forwarder IP address
Show the answer

Answer: C. The TAXII connector needs the API root URL and collection ID, and a username and password if the feed requires them.

S5An analyst wants to query the current STIX-based indicators in Sentinel. Which tables hold them?

  • AThreatIntelIndicators and ThreatIntelObjects, the new tables
  • BThreatIntelligenceIndicator, the legacy table used until 2025
  • CSecurityAlert and SecurityIncident, the alert and incident tables
  • DCommonSecurityLog and Syslog, the forwarder tables in the workspace
Show the answer

Answer: A. The new schema writes indicators to ThreatIntelIndicators and ThreatIntelObjects; the legacy table stopped after July 31, 2025.

S6An application posts JSON to a custom table through the Logs Ingestion API. Which role must the app registration hold on the DCR?

  • AMonitoring Contributor, to edit the rule
  • BLog Analytics Reader, to query the table
  • CMonitoring Metrics Publisher, to send data
  • DMicrosoft Sentinel Contributor, to write incidents
Show the answer

Answer: C. The app needs Monitoring Metrics Publisher on the DCR to send data.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Which table receives CEF data?

Show the answer

CommonSecurityLog.

R2Which port does the forwarder daemon listen on?

Show the answer

UDP and TCP 514.

R3Which policy effect configures diagnostic settings automatically?

Show the answer

DeployIfNotExists.

R4What suffix does a custom table have?

Show the answer

_CL.

R5What does a remediation task do?

Show the answer

Applies the policy to existing resources.

R6Which legacy indicator table stopped ingesting after July 31, 2025?

Show the answer

ThreatIntelligenceIndicator.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Syslog and CEF Linux forwarder, rsyslog or syslog-ng, port 514; tables Syslog and CommonSecurityLog
Severity minimum level per facility collects that level and higher
Azure Activity AzureActivity table; Azure Policy at scale plus remediation task
Threat intelligence TAXII (API root, collection ID), Upload API, new tables ThreatIntelIndicators and ThreatIntelObjects
Custom tables _CL, DCR, DCE, TimeGenerated; Monitoring Metrics Publisher for ingestion apps
